headline: Encrypt chunked-upload fragments at rest
summary: Chunked (large-file) uploads now stage every fragment as ciphertext, and the database overflow merge and settings overlay adopt prototype-pollution-safe property access.

items.title: Encrypt chunked-upload fragments at rest
items.body: A large-file upload is received in chunks that are staged on the scratch disk until the whole file arrives and is encrypted. Those fragments were previously written as plaintext for the duration of the upload — and up to a day for an abandoned upload before cleanup. Each chunk is now stored as XChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext under a per-upload key held only in memory, so no plaintext fragment ever lands on disk. An abandoned upload's on-disk fragments are unreadable ciphertext, and reassembly decrypts each chunk in order.

items.title: Prototype-pollution-safe property access on user-influenced keys
items.body: The database overflow-blob merge and the settings overlay build objects whose keys can be operator- or record-influenced. They now write and read those keys through the framework's prototype-pollution-safe own-property primitives, so a key named after a prototype member cannot re-parent the resulting object — defense-in-depth alongside the existing prototype-key stripping at parse time.
